reviews.title: Vote of no Confidence
reviews.text:
First time I use this app, I took a picture of some broccoli I have growing in my garden. I’m not sure when it is supposed to be ready to cut so I decided to look it up using Blossom and after taking two photos and uploading them, it told me it was cabbage.

reviews.title: Once great app changed by greed
reviews.text:
I genuinely used to enjoy the Blossom app—before it was acquired and aggressively monetized.

At one point, Blossom was a fantastic tool for plant identification, watering schedules, and fertilization guidance for both indoor and outdoor plants. As someone without a natural green thumb, this app was incredibly helpful. I even paid for a subscription because the value was absolutely there.

Unfortunately, that value has steadily disappeared.

Features that were once free and genuinely useful—like how much to water your plants—are now locked behind a paywall. There are also new limitations on things like alerts unless you subscribe. These changes fundamentally undermine what made the app approachable and beginner-friendly in the first place.

And then there’s the price hike.
Not a few dollars—a significant jump. Enough to make me cancel and start researching alternatives immediately. I’d recommend anyone reading this do the same, because by the time you see this review, the price may have gone up again.

I understand that AI tooling and ongoing development cost money. I’m not opposed to paying for quality software. But this no longer feels like an app designed to help people care for their plants—it feels like an app designed to extract as much money as possible.

There is still value here. But at the current price point? Absolutely not.
